_comment: policy.verify_command:
The completion gate. Until this was set, nothing checked that the suite was green
before work was marked done — the gate existed but was disarmed, so 'done' rested on
the agent's own account of it. On PR #96 that produced a task reported complete
against a tree that failed CI.
`make verify` is the right command because it is already what CONTRIBUTING points at
and it needs no cluster, cloud or database credentials: build, the full unit suite,
golangci-lint, the SPDX header policy and the manifest gates. Integration and E2E are
deliberately NOT in it — they need `make infra-up`, so a machine without Docker
Compose could never satisfy the gate and the pressure would be to disable it.
Green here is necessary, not sufficient: it says nothing about whether the tests
assert anything. Mutation-check before reporting done regardless.
TDD gate exemptions — plain glob strings.
web/admin/app/**/layout.tsx:
Next.js route segment config (`export const dynamic`) and layout composition are
declarative build-time conventions with no runtime behaviour a unit test can
observe. A test here would assert that a constant equals itself.
NOTE: this exemption originally rested on two reasons, the second being that
web/admin had no test runner at all. That reason is gone — vitest now runs via
`pnpm --filter @hermes/admin test`, wired into ci-web.yml. The first reason stands
on its own, so the exemption stays; it is no longer a placeholder for missing
infrastructure.
TESTED BY: `next build` in .github/workflows/ci-web.yml. The entire effect of
`dynamic = "force-dynamic"` is on the build — without it the build tries to
prerender authenticated pages and fails. The build is the assertion, and it now
runs in CI.
